chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the one in Ihram who places his hand upon his wife without desire. He said: 'Yes, he corrects her veil upon her, and corrects her garment upon her, and her carriage.' I said: 'Does he touch her while she is in Ihram?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'The one in Ihram places his hand with desire?' He said: 'He spills the blood of a sheep.' I said: 'And if he kisses?' He said: 'This is more intense. He slaughters a camel.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.بَدَنَة: A mature camel used for sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim in Ihram who touches his wife with desire?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between mere physical contact and sexual desire (shahwah) for a male pilgrim in Ihram, establishing that simple touch is permissible while kissing or touching with desire incurs fidya. The ruling scales the expiation based on intensity, requiring a sheep for kissing and a camel (badanah) for deeper intimacy, reflecting the principle of proportional penalty in Shia fiqh. This serves as a primary textual basis for distinguishing between minor and major breaches of Ihram restrictions regarding spouses.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam placing his hand upon his wife from without desire. Heasws said: ‘Yes, he can correct her veil upon her, or he can correct her clothes upon her, and her carriage’. I said, ‘Can he touch her and she is in Ihraam?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘The one in Ihraam placing his hand with desire?’ Heasws said: ‘He should spill blood of a sheep’. I said, ‘Supposing he kisses?’ Heasws said: ‘This is more intense. He should sacrifice a camel’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram and places his hand on his wife without lust. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can secure her veil or her cloth or her carriage.’ I then asked, ‘Can he touch her while she is in the state of Ihram?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so.’ I then asked, ‘Can he place his hand on her with lust while he is in the state of Ihram?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘There is offering of one sheep on him.’ I then asked about kissing. He (the Imam) said, ‘This is more severe. He must offer one badanah for it.’”
